correctness.rationale: For f²=e_S, extensiveness fixes S pointwise, while injectivity and monotonicity isolate moving arrows inside the intervening gaps and prevent two-step moving chains. Each gap maps bijectively to a Motzkin path by domain(U), image(D), unused(H) encoding, with ordered matching. Formal summation gives M(z)/(1-uzM(z)); the algebraic square-root singularity at 1/3 yields factorial moments of Rayleigh(sqrt(2/3)), with moment determinacy, expected sqrt(pi*n/3), and the Catalan quotient rarity estimate. An independent exhaustive enumeration of 23,713 maps and every one of 1,023 idempotent fibers for n<=9 agrees; finite checks do not establish the all-n or limit results.
residual_risks: Finite n<=9 verification does not establish all n; all-n uses the explicit Motzkin bijection.
Finite coefficient checks do not establish asymptotic convergence; proof invokes analytic singularity transfer and moment determinacy.

value.rationale: The natural equation f²=e_S is classified for every partial identity of an infinite family of injective Catalan monoids. Fibers depend on exact fixed-point gaps rather than idempotent rank (e.g. n=4 singleton endpoint fibers count 4 while interior singleton fibers count 2). The new semigroup-conditioned fixed-point distribution and exponentially rare event provide natural structural and asymptotic invariants; no broader semigroup theorem or paper-sized result is claimed.
residual_risks: No result claimed for noninjective or non-order-preserving partial maps.
The scalar total is already recorded in OEIS A005773; value rests on prescribed-idempotent fibers and the conditioned law.

final_claim: For all n>=0 and S subset [n], the number of roots f^2=e_S in IC_n equals the product of Motzkin numbers indexed by fixed-point gaps; for uniform f conditioned on f^2 idempotent, K_n/sqrt(n) converges to Rayleigh(scale sqrt(2/3)), with E K_n~sqrt(pi*n/3) and event probability ~(sqrt(3)/4)n(3/4)^n.
limitations: A005773 unweighted sequence/asymptotics known; originality only in prescribed-fiber semigroup realization and conditioned law.
